speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; to help narrow this down, how long has this rash been present, and have you noticed any recent new medications, insect bites, or changes in your skincare products?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: That rash has persisted for five months despite your denial of new exposures or medications. Given the chronicity and distribution on your upper extremities, have you noticed any scaling, blisters, or specific patterns like rings or lines? Also, does the itching significantly worsen at night or with heat?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Tinea corporis (ringworm). The chronicity, bilateral distribution on the extremities, pruritus, and lack of systemic symptoms are classic for a dermatophyte infection. I am requesting a Wood's lamp exam and KOH preparation to confirm the diagnosis.
